18	---
19	
20	## 2. Cart Page (CAI-006 – CAI-017)
21	
22	- Per line item: image, name, colour, size, price (was/now), quantity controls (increment/decrement — CAI-007), item total
23	- Actions per line item: Remove, Move to Wishlist (CAI-008)
24	- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-008). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
25	- Order summary: item count, subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront), shipping (TBC at checkout), tax where applicable, grand total in local currency (CAI-009)
26	- Promo code field (CAI-011) and Checkout CTA (CAI-010)
27	- Empty cart message shown when cart is empty (CAI-012)
28	- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) per order — error displayed if exceeded (CAI-017)
29	- Price changes while item is in cart are automatically reflected; no customer notification required (CAI-016)
30	- Sale pricing (was/now) displayed consistently across mini-cart and cart page (CAI-013)
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)
35	
36	- **Guest cart:** persisted for **30 days**
37	- **Logged-in cart:** persisted **indefinitely**
38	- **Cart merge on login:** if a guest adds items and then logs in during checkout, carts are merged (CFD-006)
39	- **Separate bag per storefront** — a customer's AU bag and US bag are independent (CRM-170)
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 4. Wishlist (CAI-018, CRM)
44	
45	- Wishlist requires authentication — guests attempting to save are redirected to login (CAI-018)
46	- **Size-level** wishlist; single global wishlist; one size per product
47	- 18-month inactivity cleanup
48	- Shareable via email
49	- Back-in-stock notifications from wishlist items
50	- Guest wishlist (with merge on login) is **out of scope for go-live** — captured in the enhancement log (CAI-018, ENH-039)
51	- **Wishlist hosting platform (SFCC vs Omneo) is being sized, not confirmed** — see Open Items (ENH-038/039). The Move-to-Wishlist login-prompt behaviour (CAI-004/008) is independent of where the wishlist is ultimately stored.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)
56	
57	### Feeds
58	- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
59	- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
60	- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
61	- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.
62	
63	### Buffer stock
64	- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
65	- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.
66	- Business users can set buffer stock via bulk upload (by category, colour, store view).
67	- **ADD TO BAG** shown when variant stock exceeds buffer threshold (CAI-026)
68	- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when stock is above zero but at or below buffer threshold; Add to Bag disabled and back-in-stock capture presented (CAI-027)
69	- **OUT OF STOCK** also shown when variant stock is fully depleted; same disabled state and back-in-stock capture (CAI-028)
70	- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)
71	- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP (CAI-031)
72	
73	### General availability vs. boutique stock
74	- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
75	- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 6. Reservation (CAI-032 – CAI-036)
80	
81	- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart
82	- **Hard reservation** only at order placement
83	- Real-time inventory check via NewStore/MuleSoft when customer proceeds from cart → checkout entry; desired behaviour confirmed, but a new MuleSoft flow is required as none currently exists — see Open Items (CAI-034)
84	- If an item is OOS at checkout entry: Checkout CTA is disabled; customer must remove the item. No auto-removal (CAI-035/036)
85	- Cart notifies customer when an item becomes OOS while in cart (CAI-035)
86	
87	---
88

90	
91	- Button shown on PDP for eligible products
92	- Opens as a flyout panel (CAI-037)
93	- On open: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft once a size has been selected (the call is per-size and refreshes when the customer selects a different size — CAI-038)
94	- No auto-refresh while the flyout panel is open
95	- Per-boutique availability for the currently selected size: **In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock** (CAI-039)
96	- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory; true physical NewStore OMS stock levels are displayed (CAI-040)
97	- Boutique stock cached with a configurable TTL (set in Business Manager — CAI-042)
98	- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
99	- *Open item: location-aware fallback (serve inventory from a nearby boutique based on user location) flagged as a potential post-launch enhancement (CAI-041, to discuss)*
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 8. Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (CAI-043 – CAI-045)
104	
105	*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*
106	
107	- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)
108	- On order placement, the order is submitted to NewStore OMS with the selected boutique as the fulfilment location; NewStore routes and assigns to boutique staff (CAI-044)
109	- Collect in Boutique availability responses cached on initial OMS call, refreshed on TTL expiry; TTL configurable in Business Manager (CAI-045)
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)
114	
115	- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
116	- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
117	- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)
118	- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers
119	
120	---
121	
122	## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)
123	
124	- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
125	- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
126	- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
127	- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")
128	
129	---
130	
131	## 11. No-Split Orders (CFD-033, CAI-033)
132	
133	- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address
134	- Customer is informed post-purchase if items ship in multiple parcels (via Narvar)
135	
136	---
137	
138	## 12. Open Items
139	
140	- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". Treat platform (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) as undecided. **FLAG — cross-sheet contradiction:** Third_Party_Integrations (Search and Recommendations / Salesforce Einstein) states the system "will use Salesforce Einstein for all search, merchandising and product recommendation functionality across all storefronts," which contradicts CAI-005 treating the engine as unconfirmed. Do not silently resolve — confirm with Zimmermann which sheet is authoritative.
141	- **CAI-023 — MuleSoft warehouse + boutique aggregation feasibility.** IC: "We had a requirement that for a SKU/size to be considered 'in stock' then it would take into account an aggregated view of warehouse & boutique stock... Will Mulesoft be able to do this?" SFCC OOTB does not aggregate; aggregation capability pending confirmation.
142	- **CAI-034 — Real-time cart→checkout inventory check requires new MuleSoft flow.** "Currently the Mulesoft does not exists for this, and will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed." Behaviour desired/confirmed, build dependency open.
143	- **CAI-041 — Location-aware boutique fallback.** RJ: "We need to consider the users location and we could potentially serve inventory from a nearby boutique." Potential post-launch enhancement.
144	- **CAI-037/039 — Find in Boutique design marked Phase 2.** Requirement Confirmed; designs not yet available for go-live timing.
145	- **ENH-038 / ENH-039 — SFCC-hosted wishlist being scoped (not confirmed).** Previously out of scope (wishlist to migrate to Omneo); both enhancements now flipped — ENH-038 (add OOS products to wishlist from PLP) Zimm response: *"ACN to size — wishlist in SFCC"*; ENH-039 (guest wishlist consolidating on login) Zimm response: *"ACN to size"* / *"To be sized"*. A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being sized but not confirmed. The Move-to-Wishlist behaviour (CAI-004/008) depends on whether the wishlist ultimately lives in SFCC vs Omneo (cf. ENH-040, which logs the SFCC→Omneo migration as a separate enhancement). Both still status "Under Review" — confirm hosting platform and go-live scope with Zimmermann before build.

## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)

- **Cart merge on login:** if a guest adds items and then logs in during checkout, carts are merged (CFD-006)

## 4. Wishlist (CAI-018, CRM)

## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)

MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

- No auto-refresh while the flyout panel is open
- Per-boutique availability for the currently selected size: **In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock** (CAI-039)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory; true physical NewStore OMS stock levels are displayed (CAI-040)
- Boutique stock cached with a configurable TTL (set in Business Manager — CAI-042)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- *Open item: location-aware fallback (serve inventory from a nearby boutique based on user location) flagged as a potential post-launch enhancement (CAI-041, to discuss)*

---

## 8. Collect in Boutique / BOPIS (CAI-043 – CAI-045)

*Scope: UK, AU, EU domestic storefronts only.*

- Real-time call to NewStore OMS via MuleSoft when the customer selects Collect in Boutique, validating both store eligibility and stock availability for the selected item and size (CAI-043)
- On order placement, the order is submitted to NewStore OMS with the selected boutique as the fulfilment location; NewStore routes and assigns to boutique staff (CAI-044)
- Collect in Boutique availability responses cached on initial OMS call, refreshed on TTL expiry; TTL configurable in Business Manager (CAI-045)

---

## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)

- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)
- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers

---

## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)

- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")

---

## 11. No-Split Orders (CFD-033, CAI-033)

- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address
- Customer is informed post-purchase if items ship in multiple parcels (via Narvar)

---

## 12. Open Items

- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". Treat platform (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) as undecided. **FLAG — cross-sheet contradiction:** Third_Party_Integrations (Search and Recommendations / Salesforce Einstein) states the system "will use Salesforce Einstein for all search, merchandising and product recommendation functionality across all storefronts," which contradicts CAI-005 treating the engine as unconfirmed. Do not silently resolve — confirm with Zimmermann which sheet is authoritative.
- **CAI-023 — MuleSoft warehouse + boutique aggregation feasibility.** IC: "We had a requirement that for a SKU/size to be considered 'in stock' then it would take into account an aggregated view of warehouse & boutique stock... Will Mulesoft be able to do this?" SFCC OOTB does not aggregate; aggregation capability pending confirmation.
- **CAI-034 — Real-time cart→checkout inventory check requires new MuleSoft flow.** "Currently the Mulesoft does not exists for this, and will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed." Behaviour desired/confirmed, build dependency open.
- **CAI-041 — Location-aware boutique fallback.** RJ: "We need to consider the users location and we could potentially serve inventory from a nearby boutique." Potential post-launch enhancement.
- **CAI-037/039 — Find in Boutique design marked Phase 2.** Requirement Confirmed; designs not yet available for go-live timing.
- **ENH-038 / ENH-039 — SFCC-hosted wishlist being scoped (not confirmed).** Previously out of scope (wishlist to migrate to Omneo); both enhancements now flipped — ENH-038 (add OOS products to wishlist from PLP) Zimm response: *"ACN to size — wishlist in SFCC"*; ENH-039 (guest wishlist consolidating on login) Zimm response: *"ACN to size"* / *"To be sized"*. A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being sized but not confirmed. The Move-to-Wishlist behaviour (CAI-004/008) depends on whether the wishlist ultimately lives in SFCC vs Omneo (cf. ENH-040, which logs the SFCC→Omneo migration as a separate enhancement). Both still status "Under Review" — confirm hosting platform and go-live scope with Zimmermann before build.

880	`text.muted = grey[300] = #969696` and **no `subtlest`**. Both Figma names collapse onto
881	**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
882	**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
883	| Figma | Ours |
884	|---|---|
885	| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
886	| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
887	| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
888	| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
889	| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
890	| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
891	| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |
892	
893	**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
894	state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
895	- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
896	  (regular/400, ls 0)
897	- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
898	  where the gutter should be 32px
899	- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
900	- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
901	Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
902	=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
903	   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.
904	
905	**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
906	("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
907	("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
908	the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
909	**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
910	information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
911	specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.
912	
913	**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
914	- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
915	  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
916	  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the
917	  mobile cart item image. Same token, different fallback => the decimal is what Figma rendered after
918	  scaling, not the token value. **Use the token (48 / 40), never the decimal.**
919	- **Tablet 659.2 is a computed fill width, not a spec.** `659.2 = 595.2 content + 2 × 32 gutter`;
920	  the gutter is a real token (32px). Confirmed NOT a uniformly scaled instance — the tablet header
921	  is its own 92px and the message band is exactly 52 (unscaled).
922	  **Implement tablet as a fluid width with a 32px gutter, never a hardcoded 659.2.**
923	
924	### Responsive rule (derived)
925	| | Panel | Layout | Gutter | Header |
926	|---|---|---|---|---|
927	| Desktop 1440+ | **fixed 1186px** | two-column (items 360 / totals 430, 140 gutter) | 128 | 84 |
928	| Tablet 834 | fluid (~79%) | **single column** | **32** | 92 |
929	| Mobile 402 | full-width | single column | 32 | 108 (68 in some states — drift) |
930	
931	### Additional drift found while resolving these
932	- **The mobile message band hardcodes `px-[128px]` across multiple states** — should be 32px.
933	  Systematic, not a one-off.
934	- **Mobile header height varies by state**: 108 (default) vs 68 (error states).
935	- **Within a single node, one message is `w-full` and the next is `w-[476px]`** (mobile

938	## 11.11 Final three design items — SETTLED (Marcel, 2026-09-16). None go to the designer as questions.
939	
940	**(1) Stepper touch target — BUILD 24px.** Wrap each 12x12 glyph in an invisible 24x24 centred box.

file.content:
`text.muted = grey[300] = #969696` and **no `subtlest`**. Both Figma names collapse onto
**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
| Figma | Ours |
|---|---|
| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |

**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
  (regular/400, ls 0)
- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
  where the gutter should be 32px
- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.

**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.

**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the
  mobile cart item image. Same token, different fallback => the decimal is what Figma rendered after
  scaling, not the token value. **Use the token (48 / 40), never the decimal.**
- **Tablet 659.2 is a computed fill width, not a spec.** `659.2 = 595.2 content + 2 × 32 gutter`;
  the gutter is a real token (32px). Confirmed NOT a uniformly scaled instance — the tablet header
  is its own 92px and the message band is exactly 52 (unscaled).
  **Implement tablet as a fluid width with a 32px gutter, never a hardcoded 659.2.**

### Responsive rule (derived)
| | Panel | Layout | Gutter | Header |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 1440+ | **fixed 1186px** | two-column (items 360 / totals 430, 140 gutter) | 128 | 84 |
| Tablet 834 | fluid (~79%) | **single column** | **32** | 92 |
| Mobile 402 | full-width | single column | 32 | 108 (68 in some states — drift) |

### Additional drift found while resolving these
- **The mobile message band hardcodes `px-[128px]` across multiple states** — should be 32px.
  Systematic, not a one-off.
- **Mobile header height varies by state**: 108 (default) vs 68 (error states).
- **Within a single node, one message is `w-full` and the next is `w-[476px]`** (mobile
  warnings-hidden). Clear drift.

## 11.11 Final three design items — SETTLED (Marcel, 2026-09-16). None go to the designer as questions.

**(1) Stepper touch target — BUILD 24px.** Wrap each 12x12 glyph in an invisible 24x24 centred box.
Justified three ways independently: our own atoms already use 24 (`zimmButton`, `zimmTextInput`,
`zimmNavItem`, `footerNavColumn` — all `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), the design's own node is literally
named `touchTarget` at 24, and WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 sets 24 as the minimum (AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA).
Use `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size — it is already `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, and its comment
explains why it must be minW/minH rather than padding (Chakra `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0`
as a style prop that merges after `__css`, so recipe padding is silently dropped).
**Gap: use 8px (`xs`)** -> 14px apparent, since a 24 box adds 6px invisible padding each side and
there is no 6px token (scale jumps 4 -> 8 -> 12). 4 and 8 are equidistant from the design's 12;
8 is chosen because erring toward more space is correct for a touch control.

1. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` from the repo root. Paste the real output (or confirm it's clean with zero errors — quote the actual terminal output, don't summarize).

Label findings CONFIRMED (you reproduced it) or PLAUSIBLE. Keep your final report factual and complete with real pasted output — it will be read directly by the coordinating tester, not summarized further before use as evidence.

- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts

- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/css.md

Your job, specifically:

1. **Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`** (or `npm run audit:tokens`) and read its real output. It's advisory (not CI-gated) — report only NEW findings in the touched files (the zimmCartDrawer folder and the 2-line index.ts addition), not pre-existing findings elsewhere in the repo that aren't this step's fault. Note: the recipe file has an explicit `audit-allow:` comment for `ITEMS_COLUMN_WIDTH`/`TOTALS_COLUMN_WIDTH` (360px/430px raw rem values) — check whether the audit script actually recognizes and downgrades that per its own acknowledged-exception rule (`provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow:` in the surrounding comment block), or whether it still flags it as a failure despite the comment.

2. **Semantic intent check**: for every `var(--zimm-color-*)` used in the new files, verify the semantic category matches the CSS property it's applied to (text.*/icon.* on `color:`, background.* on `background:`/`bg:`, border.* on `border-color:`). Note: this recipe/component may not use ANY `--zimm-color-*` vars at all (it looked spacing/sizing-only on first read) — if so, say that plainly and call this sub-check vacuous/clean rather than padding the report.

3. **Bare Chakra token key check**: confirm no bare theme-scale key (e.g. `paddingInline: '2xl'` instead of `paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'`) appears anywhere in the new recipe or component files. Cross-check against `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — read that test file to understand exactly what it mechanically checks, then verify by inspection that zimmCartDrawer.css.ts would actually pass it (don't just assume — check the recipe's structure, especially the media-query-keyed sub-objects, against whatever traversal logic recipeGuards.test.ts uses; there's a chance a nested media-query key structure isn't walked the same way a flat baseStyle is).

4. **Raw literal check**: confirm there is no raw hex/px value used where a rem-based token should be, per overrideStyling.md's Units section. The recipe has two audit-allowed raw rem constants (22.5rem/26.875rem = 360px/430px) with a comment citing "pending a foundation token" — confirm that comment is actually present and properly formatted per the audit script's own recognized vocabulary (re-read the comment block above those two consts).

5. **Recipe namespacing**: confirm the recipe key `ZimmCartDrawer` is properly Zimm-namespaced (not reusing/mutating a base Chakra recipe name) and registered correctly in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (both imported AND included in the exported `components` object — check both, a partial registration is a real bug).

6. **Recipe state exhaustiveness check (from the standing angle list)**: for every part in this recipe (`messages`, `body`, `footer`), check whether any of them are actually interactive (cursor:pointer, onClick, onKeyDown) — if none are, say explicitly that this sub-check is vacuous for this recipe (a shell of layout-only divs) rather than leaving it unaddressed, and drop it rather than force a finding.

7. **Hover-gating correctness check (from the standing angle list)**: check whether this recipe has any hidden-by-default part revealed on hover/focus. If not (this looks like a pure responsive-layout recipe with no interaction-gated reveal), say so explicitly and drop this angle rather than leaving it unverified.

8. **Units discipline**: confirm rem is used for anything spacing/type-related, and that the two provisional column-width consts are commented as required (see overrideStyling.md's Units section).

Do not fix anything. Do not touch any file. Report CONFIRMED (you verified it directly, e.g. by running the script or reading the exact test traversal logic) or PLAUSIBLE, and say what you tried to falsify (e.g. did you actually try to think of a way the recipe's media-query nesting could slip past recipeGuards.test.ts's bare-key check, or did you just assume it wouldn't) and what you couldn't verify. If an angle is genuinely clean or vacuous, say so in one line rather than padding — don't manufacture findings. Your report will be read directly by the coordinating tester as evidence, so include real command output where you ran commands.

input.prompt:
You are one of four parallel testers checking a single implemented build step in the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (branch feature/SFCC-11_cart, working tree, NOT committed). The step is SFCC-315, a new `ZimmCartDrawer` organism at overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/. Playwright is already a project dependency (used for e2e/tests) — you do not need to install anything new; check package.json/playwright.config for the installed version and reuse it (e.g. `npx playwright test` or drive it via a standalone script with `require('playwright')`/`import {chromium} from 'playwright'`). Use your scratchpad directory /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/6017b702-06fb-4295-9164-1c708495531a/scratchpad for any throwaway script/spec files — do not add files to the actual repo.

YOUR LANE ONLY: real, live-rendered-layout verification of one specific, disputed responsive-breakpoint question. Three other agents are separately covering: compiles-and-passes, tokens/styling-conformance, and structure/imports/a11y/DRY. Not your job — don't touch those.

## Background you need

Read these 2 files first, in full:
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts (the `body` part's `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})` block is the one in question — `breakpoints.xl` = 1280px, defined in overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts)

Also read the Storybook story: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx — it exports a `Default` story (itemCount=3) rendering `ZimmCartDrawer` pre-opened (`isOpen` starts `true` via local `useState`).

Also read overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts's `xLarge` variant styling (the outer drawer panel ZimmCartDrawer renders inside) — it sets the panel to a fixed `74.125rem` (1186px) width with `maxWidth: '100%'`, applying from the `md` breakpoint (768px) up. So below 1186px viewport width the panel is clamped narrower than 1186px; at/above 1186px the panel is exactly 1186px.

## The dispute

The recipe's `body` part switches from a single-column flex layout to a two-column CSS grid (`gridTemplateColumns: '22.5rem 26.875rem'` = 360px/430px, with a 140px column gap and 128px inline padding on each side — total required content width 360+430+140+2×128 = 1186px) at `breakpoints.xl` = 1280px viewport width. But a separate planning document (.claude/session-notes.md, already read by the coordinating tester — you don't need to re-read the whole file) contains a table titled "Responsive rule (derived)" stating the two-column desktop layout should start at "Desktop 1440+", not 1280. There is no Figma frame evidence for anything between a 834px-wide "tablet" frame (single column) and a 1440px-wide "desktop" frame (two column) — so there's a genuine ~160px zone (1280–1439px) where the built code and the plan's stated threshold disagree, with no direct design evidence either way.

## Your job

1. Get the `Default` story of `Layout/ZimmCartDrawer` (or wherever it's actually filed — check the story's own `title` field) rendering in a real browser. The most reliable path: `npm run build-storybook` (can take a couple of minutes), then serve the static output (e.g. `npx http-server storybook-static -p <free-port> --silent &` or `npx serve storybook-static -p <free-port>` — pick a port unlikely to collide) and open the story directly via its iframe URL: `http://localhost:<port>/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&viewMode=story` (Storybook's story id is a slugified `title--exportName`, e.g. roughly `layout-zimmcartdrawer--default` — confirm the exact id from `storybook-static/index.json` or by grepping the built output if the guess doesn't resolve). If build-storybook is too slow, `npm run storybook` (dev server, default port 6006) is an acceptable fallback — just make sure whichever you use is fully ready (poll until the port responds) before driving Playwright at it.
2. Using real Playwright (a real Chromium instance, not jsdom), for EACH of these viewport widths — 1186, 1280, 1350, 1440, and 1500 (use a tall-enough height, e.g. 1200px, so nothing is height-constrained) — load the Default story fresh and measure, with real `getBoundingClientRect()` / computed style calls against the actual DOM (not by reading the recipe source or doing arithmetic):
   - The actual rendered width of the drawer panel (the outermost drawer content element — find it via its role, e.g. `getByRole('dialog')`, then `.boundingBox()`).
   - Whether the body content area is actually laid out as a CSS grid (two columns) or a single flex column at that width — read the real computed `display` and, if grid, the real computed `grid-template-columns` value (via `element.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).display)` etc.), not an assumption from the stylesheet source.
   - If it IS in two-column mode, measure the actual rendered widths of the two column children and the gap between them, and check whether anything overflows — compare the dialog's own `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` (does content overflow horizontally?) and check for any visual clipping (e.g. compute whether the two children's combined width + gap + padding exceeds the actual panel's rendered width).
3. Report, per viewport width, in a table: viewport width | measured panel width | single-column or two-column (real computed value) | any overflow/clipping detected (yes/no + numbers) | anything visually cramped or broken.
4. State plainly: at exactly which viewport width does the real rendered behavior switch from single-column to two-column? Does this match 1280 (the code) as expected, or something else? Is there any broken/overflowing/cramped rendering anywhere in the 1186–1439px zone specifically (the disputed range)?
5. Try to falsify the "it's fine because 1186 = exactly the two-column content's minimum required width" arithmetic claim — actually check whether the panel is really at least 1186px wide by the time the grid engages (i.e. confirm empirically that the ZimmDrawer panel's own separate breakpoint reaches full 1186px width at or before wherever the two-column grid switch engages, so the grid never has less room than it needs) rather than trusting the arithmetic.

Report real measured numbers, not calculations, for every row. If you cannot get a real browser to render Storybook at all in this environment, say so explicitly, explain exactly what you tried and where it failed, and state clearly that this means the breakpoint question remains unverified by live rendering — do not fall back to reporting arithmetic as if it were a live measurement, and do not guess. Label everything CONFIRMED (you personally measured it) vs anything you had to infer. End with what you tried to falsify and what you could not verify.

### SFCC-272 — Remove and Wishlist Actions · 8 ACs · 8 of 8 deliverable

ACs — Remove (3): item removed with drawer count decrementing and totals updating; removing the last
item shows the empty state "as per SFCC-277"; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
Wishlist (5): authenticated qty 1 → moved, removed from cart, count decrements, totals update,
**page-level success banner** "[Product Name] has been moved to your wishlist"; authenticated qty > 1
→ all units removed, a single SKU saved, count decrements by the full quantity, same banner;
already in wishlist → **page-level error banner** "Selected product already exists in wishlist and
the item remains in the cart"; guest → redirected to login/registration, item stays in cart;
guest authenticates → returns, item moved, success banner at top of cart.

Decisions:
- **Message surface: base Chakra toast as the interim.** All messages emitted through **one** handler
  so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. Use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not
  the base hook. Marker comment naming SFCC-404 at the emit site.
  - Consequence (good): with a toast, the message **behaviour and copy** are delivered, so what's
    deferred is presentation only, not functionality. AC6 — whose entire observable outcome is the
    error message — becomes deliverable.
  - Word the Jira comment as *"message behaviour and copy delivered; surface deferred to SFCC-404"*,
    **not** "AC met" — the ACs say page-level banner and a toast is not one.
  - There is no cart override today, so the toast is being *implemented*, not inherited. Not free.
  - Chakra toasts portal to `document.body`, outside `canvasElement`. A Storybook `play` asserting a
    message must use `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing the portal exception —
    `testing.md` sanctions that specifically and nowhere else.

Two need a flag: - **AC7 (focus returned to trigger) — see the dedicated FocusLock finding below.** - **AC9 (responsive per Figma) — see the dedicated breakpoint finding below.** - **AC8 (no loss of scroll position) — 🔵 note, PLAUSIBLE.** The new test pins a real `window.scrollY` and asserts it survives the open/close cycle — a real improvement over just checking `overflow` unlocked. But jsdom cannot simulate real scroll physics at all, so this test can only prove "nothing in this code path calls `window.scrollTo`" (true, and worth having), not "a real browser's layout doesn't shift when `overflow:hidden` toggles on/off ``" — a documented mobile Safari quirk this layer structurally cannot exercise either way. Not a confirmed bug, just a real limit on what was actually proven. One scope note that's *not* a finding: SFCC-315's own scope boundary ("315 owns the empty-state header text only — the empty body is SFCC-277's," session-notes.md line 292) is respected — the inline `EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT` is clearly commented as temporary scaffolding, not a real empty-state build. I initially suspected this might violate a "build the empty state as a discrete component" instruction elsewhere in the plan, but traced that instruction to session-notes.md's SFCC-272 section (a different ticket, different scenario — removing the last item mid-session) — doesn't apply here. No violation. ## 9. Story interactivity fidelity — vacuous, clean Neither `Default` nor `Empty` exposes a live picker/toggle/selector via args — they're two separate stories with a fixed `itemCount` each, not one story with a user-changeable control. The one piece of real interactivity (`isOpen`/`onClose`) genuinely is wired to local `useState` in the story wrapper (`CartDrawerExample`), so it's structurally capable of updating — there's just no control surface for this specific fidelity bug to exist in. Checked, not padded. ## 10. Real rendered-layout verification — the breakpoint question, resolved live **CONFIRMED by a dedicated real-Chromium Playwright run** (via `build-storybook` + a static server, driven twice independently with byte-identical results), at viewports 1186/1279/1280/1350/1440/1500: | Viewport | Panel width | Body layout | Grid columns/gap/padding | Overflow | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1186 | 1186px | flex (1-col) | n/a | none | | 1279 | 1186px | flex (1-col) | n/a | none | | **1280** | 1186px | **grid (2-col)** | 360px / 430px, 140px gap, 128px padding | none | | 1350–1500 | 1186px | grid (2-col) | same | none | **The exact live switch point is 1279→1280px — matching the shipped code's `breakpoints.xl` exactly, not the plan's stated threshold.** This resolves the brief's judgment call with a fact I found independently, not just live-rendering the ambiguity: `.claude/session-notes.md`'s own "Responsive rule (derived)" table (§11.10, "Desktop 1440+ | fixed 1186px | two-column...") is a dedicated, explicit responsive-threshold decision — not a stray Figma-frame citation like the `WIDTH_XLARGE` precedent the Implementer reasoned from. That precedent (`zimmDrawer.css.ts:28-38`) is genuinely a "no threshold decision" case: the panel measures **identically** (1186px) at both the 1440px and 1920px Figma frames, so there was nothing to decide. Here, by contrast, the plan's derived rule is explicitly choosing a switch point between two *different* layout states (single-column at the 834px tablet frame vs. two-column at the 1440px desktop frame) — and there is no Figma frame anywhere between 834 and 1440 to arbitrate where that switch should actually land. So this isn't the same "just a citation, not a decision" situation the Implementer's own precedent-reasoning describes — it's a genuine 160px conflict between what the plan document says (1440+) and what shipped (1280), with no design evidence on either side of the gap. Separately, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:3-7` shows the codebase *does* have a real precedent for snapping a "1440px-cited frame" onto an existing alias (`lg`, not literally 1440) rather than inventing a new breakpoint — so reusing `xl` isn't an unreasonable engineering choice, just one that conflicts with this specific plan's own explicit text, with nothing to prove which is "right." **This needs an authoritative call (designer/PM), not a testing verdict** — flagging as 🟡 should-fix / possibly 🔴 depending on how strictly AC9 is read, CONFIRMED conflict, not CONFIRMED broken. No overflow, clipping, or visual breakage found anywhere in the disputed 1280–1439px zone — the "1186 = exact minimum required width" arithmetic was independently falsified-and-held: the drawer panel is already pinned at exactly 1186px starting at 1186px viewport width itself (a full 94–512px before the grid engages), so the grid never has less room than it needs, confirmed by direct measurement rather than trusted arithmetic. The only visible difference at 1280 vs. 1279 is the placeholder sentence wrapping from 1 to 2 lines inside the narrower 360px column — expected text reflow of throwaway placeholder content, not a defect. ## FocusLock finding (AC7) — sanity-checked against real library source, holds up **CONFIRMED as an architectural fact** (traced through actual installed source in `node_modules/@chakra-ui/modal/dist/index.js`, `node_modules/@chakra-ui/focus-lock/dist/index.js`, `node_modules/react-focus-lock/dist/cjs/Trap.js` — not relayed from the Implementer's description): `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx`'s `` call (line 236-242) never passes `finalFocusRef` to Chakra's own `` — it's only used manually inside `handleCloseComplete` (line 231-233), invoked via `onCloseComplete`. Chakra's `Modal` (`@chakra-ui/modal/dist/index.js:235-277`) defaults `returnFocusOnClose: true` and reads `finalFocusRef` purely from its own props — since it's never passed, it's `undefined` inside Chakra's own context. `ModalFocusScope` (same file, line 291-320) forwards that `undefined` straight into `@chakra-ui/focus-lock`'s wrapper as `finalFocusRef={undefined}, restoreFocus={true}`; that wrapper computes `returnFocus = restoreFocus && !finalFocusRef` = `true`, and `react-focus-lock`'s real `Trap.js` restores focus via its own native mechanism on deactivation, completely independent of Zimmermann's manual call. **Consequence:** there are genuinely two uncoordinated focus-restoration mechanisms active on every close — Chakra's own native "return to whatever had focus when the trap activated" and Zimmermann's manual `finalFocusRef.current.focus()`. They only agree by coincidence when the trigger really did hold keyboard focus before opening — exactly the case `finalFocusRef` exists to handle when it *isn't* guaranteed (programmatic opens, opens triggered from a differently-focused element). Whether Chakra's native restore actually wins the timing race in a real browser is something I could not instrument live (matching the Implementer's own honest caveat) — that specific consequence is PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED. But the underlying architecture — two independent, non-communicating focus-restore paths — is CONFIRMED, not speculative. This is pre-existing code (`zimmDrawer/index.tsx`), correctly out of scope to fix in this commit, but it's the mechanism this ticket's own AC7 depends on, and every existing test of it (including this commit's own) opens the drawer via a genuine click on the exact `finalFocusRef` target — so no test in the repo can currently distinguish "AC7 works because of the manual call" from "AC7 works because of a lucky coincidence." UNIFORM: this affects every current `ZimmDrawer` consumer that passes `finalFocusRef`, not just cart. ## Visual checkpoint table | What to check | Figma reference | Expected value | How to verify | |---|---|---|---| | Messages band min-height | `Cart-level-messages` frame (session-notes.md §11.3 — no numeric node-id recorded in the plan doc, frame name only) | 52px (`--zimm-scale-1300`) | DevTools computed `min-height` on the `messages` part | | Messages/body/footer gutter, mobile+tablet | `cart/drawer/mobile` (402w) / `cart/drawer/tablet` (834w) | 32px (`--zimm-scale-2xl`) | DevTools computed `padding-inline` below 1280px — CONFIRMED live | | Messages/body/footer gutter, desktop | `cart/drawer/xlarge`/`large` (1920w/1440w) | 128px (`--zimm-scale-6xl`) | DevTools computed `padding-inline` at/above 1280px (code) — plan says at/above 1440px, see conflict above | | Body layout, mobile/tablet | `cart/drawer/tablet` | single-column, flex | CONFIRMED live at 1186–1279px | | Body layout, desktop | `cart/drawer/xlarge`/`large` | two-column grid, 360px/430px, 140px gap | CONFIRMED live at ≥1280px | | Drawer panel width, desktop | `cart/drawer/xlarge`/`large` | fixed 1186px | CONFIRMED live, exactly 1186px across 1186–1500px | | Two-column switch threshold | **no Figma frame exists between the 834px and 1440px frames** | UNRESOLVED — plan text says 1440+, shipped code and live render agree on 1280 | Open question — needs a designer/PM call, not further testing | | Header height (desktop/mobile) | `drawer/header` frame, 84px/108px | Inherited from `ZimmDrawer`, not re-verified this pass | Out of scope this commit — flagging as unverified, not assumed correct | --- ## What I tried to falsify Across the four sub-agents and my own work: traced the backdrop-click DOM claim against real `ZimmDrawer` source instead of trusting the test's comment; hand-traced `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s actual traversal logic against this recipe's nested-`@media`-key shape instead of trusting a green suite; traced `auditTokenUsage.mjs`'s own blank-line-boundary matching logic against the real file instead of trusting its printed bucket; grepped every sibling organism's story `title:` to check whether "Layout/" was a defensible norm or an outlier (it's an outlier); checked whether `ZimmDrawer` has its own equivalent test coverage before calling the 5 close-mechanic tests "duplication" (found it doesn't, for 4 of 5); rendered the real component in a real browser at 6 widths, twice independently, instead of trusting the recipe's own arithmetic; traced the FocusLock claim through 3 actual installed package sources instead of relaying the Implementer's description; and verified `git status` myself, twice, rather than trusting the Implementer's file list. ## What I could not verify - Whether Chakra's native focus-restore actually wins the timing race against the manual `handleCloseComplete` call in a real browser — confirmed the architecture is a real, uncoordinated dual-path, but not the practical winner, without live instrumentation beyond this pass's scope. - The "right" answer to the 1280-vs-1440 breakpoint dispute — no Figma frame exists between 834 and 1440 viewport width, so no amount of testing resolves which threshold is actually intended; this needs a design/PM decision. - `ZimmDrawer`'s own inherited behaviors (AC1's right-aligned X, AC4's slide-from-right, AC5's overlay/mobile-full-screen) — not re-verified fresh this pass, relied on their having been correct when built in an earlier commit. - Whether `zimmPdpDrawer`/`zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`/`zimmAuthDrawerContent` currently pass `finalFocusRef` at their own call sites (i.e., whether they're live-exposed to the FocusLock gap today) — traced the mechanism generically, didn't re-check each consumer's call site individually. - `messages`/`footer` parts' behavior at the disputed breakpoint got only an incidental visual read (footer's inset visibly shifting at the same 1280px threshold) from the Playwright agent, not the same rigorous measurement given to `body`. ## What Marcel is missing The FocusLock gap isn't cart-specific — it's a latent defect in the shared `ZimmDrawer` atom that every current consumer passing `finalFocusRef` (PDP drawer, wishlist auth drawer, auth drawer content) already ships with today, and it's invisible to the entire test suite because every existing test — including this new one — happens to open the drawer via a real click on the exact element `finalFocusRef` points to, so the coincidence and the real mechanism can never be told apart by any test that exists right now. Worth a dedicated spike/ticket before it's found the hard way (a non-click open path, or an AT user) rather than waiting for the next drawer commit to re-surface it. ## Relevant files - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx` - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.test.tsx` - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx` (out of scope, referenced for the FocusLock/breakpoint findings) - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/session-notes.md` (source of the AC list and the "Responsive rule (derived)" breakpoint conflict)
